answer: Moshi’s architecture is built from three core parts: a custom text language‑model backbone called Helium, a neural audio codec named Mimi that uses residual vector quantization and distills semantic knowledge from a self‑supervised speech model, and a streaming, hierarchical generator that produces semantic and acoustic tokens for both the user and Moshi while aligning Moshi’s text tokens (Inner Monologue) [Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue, arXiv:2410.00037v1, PDF p. 6].
